questions.q: What does O'Brien say the media did during the Brexit campaign?
a: It gave far more coverage to the leave side
It gave equal time to both campaigns
It refused to cover the referendum
It backed remaining in the EU
questions.why: Lesson one says leavers received more airtime and column space, which pushed undecided readers toward their view.

questions.q: What effect did media focus on Muslim extremists have, according to O'Brien?
a: It tarred a whole group and boosted support for Brexit
It reduced public concern about immigration
It improved reporting standards at newspapers
It led to a ban on extremist groups
questions.why: Lesson one says most immigrants were harmless, but coverage of extremists made an entire group suffer and increased Brexit votes.

questions.q: What does O'Brien say political correctness does to public debate?
a: It makes people afraid to speak their minds
It makes debates more polite and useful
It protects minority groups from harm
It encourages more honest journalism
questions.why: Lesson two argues that constant offense-taking divides people and makes them scared to say what they think.

questions.q: What does the book advise readers to do in a world of disinformation?
a: Check sources and stick to verified facts
Trust established newspapers without question
Avoid reading any political coverage
Follow the most popular voices online
questions.why: The review says the book helps readers choose reliable sources and avoid falling for mass trends.

questions.q: What is the core problem with social media opinions, according to O'Brien?
a: People share claims without the expertise to judge them
People post too rarely to influence anyone
Platforms remove too many honest opinions
Only journalists are allowed to publish news
questions.why: Lesson three says everyone can now broadcast views whether or not they understand the topic, spreading misinformation.
